issues.description: Element: SealSaloon.stock (the saloon's stock attribute). The problem statement gives contradictory instructions: problem_statement.md (lines 70-71) tells students to initialize the stock in the SealSaloon constructor (implying an instance field initialized per-constructor), but later the problem_statement.md (lines 77-80) explicitly requires the stock attribute to be static/shared across all instances. The reference solution declares the field as a static class member: solution_repository/src/de/tum/cit/ase/SealSaloon.java (line 5) declares "private static final Stock stock = new Stock();". The template's Main.java commented example uses instance-style access (template_repository/src/de/tum/cit/ase/Main.java lines 11-12 show `SealSaloon shop = new SealSaloon(); shop.getStock().setStockIngredients(...)`). This inconsistency leaves students unsure whether to implement stock as an instance field initialized in the constructor or as a static class field and how to initialize and access it.
issues.suggestedFix:
Resolve the design ambiguity in the problem statement. Either:
1) Make stock a shared static resource: update the problem statement text that currently instructs to initialize stock in the constructor to instead state that stock is a static/shared attribute (example: "private static final Stock stock = new Stock();"), and show/access it via a static getter. Remove wording that tells students to initialize stock in the constructor. Update example code comments to reflect static usage (or note that calling a static getter on an instance is allowed but discouraged).
OR
2) Make stock an instance field: remove the lines that require stock to be static (lines 77-80) and change the reference solution accordingly (move initialization into the constructor and make getStock() non-static).
Update the statement and examples consistently so students clearly know whether stock is static or instance and how to initialize and access it.
